system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A subject/placed_subject/replacement_subject reference supplies its selected identity properties, not its original background, pose or photographic lighting. An environment reference supplies its scene, not the depicted actor identity or actor-specific appearance. An observed claim copying a mixed source summary must obey the same responsibility: citing the source does not authorize importing all its content. Independently requested or creative content is allowed; a generic car or room resembling a source is not itself evidence of misuse. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. A visual source video does not wire its soundtrack. composition_facts.audio declares the actually wired audio relationships. If its attachments are empty, an explicit claim that the original soundtrack is preserved, reused, played or carried over is audio_signal_misuse even if the task prefix omits reuse. Newly generated sound is permitted and a similar sound does not demonstrate copying. Property-only voice, music-style, beat and sound-texture references condition a new sound; they do not play the original recording. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.

fragments.shot:shot-1:description: In a dark tunnel, <Subject:subject-1> rolls through deep shadow, holding a steady left-to-right course across the width of the scene. Its headlights cut a narrow cone through the gloom, picking out rough concrete walls, faint seams and drifting dust just ahead of the bumper. The car is mostly a dark silhouette at first, with only the leading edges and wheel rims catching a thin sheen from the light spill. Tyres hiss softly on the asphalt while a low engine hum fills the enclosed space and returns off the curved walls. As the seconds pass, the car gathers pace and pulls forward out of the deepest shadow, so more of its shape emerges into the lit foreground: the nose clears the dark pocket, the beam stretches farther down the tunnel, and the concrete brightens in a narrow moving pool. The car keeps travelling left to right, steady and controlled, while the contrast between the unlit distance and the advancing pool of light deepens. Cool air and fine grit hang in the beam, and the wet asphalt throws back a few broken highlights. The movement reads as a deliberate release from the dark rather than a sudden swerve.

fragments.shot:shot-2:description: In a brighter pocket of the tunnel, <Subject:subject-1> surges forward into the light and continues left to right across the scene. The headlights now reach farther, sweeping over rough concrete and a low service kerb while the car's panels flash with brief reflections from the wet asphalt. The engine note rises as it accelerates, the sound tightening in the enclosed space, and the tyres send a sharper hiss through the tunnel. The car becomes clearer and more present in the foreground: the nose pushes ahead, the wheels track through the moving pool of light, and the darker mouth of the tunnel recedes behind it. Fine grit and dust drift through the beam, and the concrete walls slide past in soft bands of shadow and illumination. The air stays cool and close, and the headlight wash gives the concrete a pale, damp sheen. The car holds its forward pull, emerging fully from the dark without changing direction. The mood stays cool, mechanical and focused, with the contrast between the lit body and the surrounding gloom carrying the sense of release.
